For the Appellant/s : Mr.Praveen Kumar, Advocate  For the Respondent/s : Mr.Abhay Kumar, APP  ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SHAILENDRA SINGH  ORAL ORDER 3 15-12-2023 1.
Heard the parties.

2. This appeal has been preferred against the judgment of conviction dated 25.01.2023 and order of sentence dated 30.01.2023 passed by the Court of learned 6 th Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum-Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Bhagalpur in connection with POCSO.

entities.text: 6 th Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum-Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Bhagalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Case No.
495 of 2015, arising out of Nathnagar P.S. Case No. 31 of 2015, whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted for the offence(s) punishable under Section(s) 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of POCSO Act and sentenced for the said offences.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant presses the prayer for bail made by the appellant in the memo of appeal under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C.
Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.916 of 2023(3) dt.15-12-2023 4.

The main submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellant are that during trial, the appellant remained on bail and since the date of conviction he has been languishing in jail and the FIR was lodged by victim's father who made false allegation in the FIR, in fact, there was friendship between the so-called victim and the appellant and admittedly the victim went to appellant's house to attend a Birthday party and next day she returned back and during that time no sexual assault Roushan Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68482800/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 was committed by the appellant and in this regard victim's statement recorded by herself under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. which was proved before the trial court, may be perused, in which she did not reveal any fact to support the allegation of the FIR, while at the time of victim's production before the Judicial Magistrate, she was not under the influence of the appellant and before the trial court she accepted that prior to recording her statement before the Judicial Magistrate she was told that she was free to record her statement and only thereafter she recorded her statement.

Further submission is that before the trial court the victim accepted that her statement was not recorded by the investigating officer during investigation and the victim's medical examination report is completely faulty as per evidence of the Doctor concerned, who was examined as Patna High Court CR.
Learned APP has opposed the bail prayer of the appellant.

6. Considering the above submissions and mainly the defences taken by the appellant discussed above and also unlikelihood of the appellant's appeal to be taken up for hearing in near future, this court is inclined to accept the bail prayer of the appellant.

Accordingly, let the appellant named-above be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.
10,000/- (ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned 6th Additional District and Sessions Judge-cum-Exclusive Special Judge, POCSO Act, Bhagalpur in connection with POCSO.

7. The realization of the fine amount imposed upon the appellant by the convicting trial court shall remain suspended during pendency of this appeal.

8. List this appeal under appropriate heading in due course.
(Shailendra Singh, J) Rajiv/-
